_why: Round 13: the same octopus facts, rewritten the way a person TELLS it (short sentences, contractions, one number), against the written lines the channel posted. Separates 'the script reads like a report' from 'the voice is robotic'.
written: Your octopus has five hundred million neurons, and three hundred twenty million of them aren't in its head.
An octopus runs on about five hundred million neurons, but only one hundred eighty million of them sit in its central brain. The other three hundred twenty million are out in its arms.

That's because every one of its two hundred eighty suckers per arm is its own touch-and-taste sensor, two thousand two hundred forty of them across all eight arms, each wired straight into that arm's own nerves.
And that control is so independent, a severed arm keeps reacting to touch and pain for up to three thousand six hundred seconds after it's cut off, a full hour, with no brain attached at all.
Data counted his own brains. Still just the one. Would you want a second brain in each arm? Tell me below.
spoken: So an octopus has about five hundred million neurons. And most of them? Not in its head.
Only about a third are in its actual brain. The rest live out in its arms.
Every sucker on every arm can touch and taste on its own. It's wired straight into that arm.
It's so independent that a cut-off arm keeps reacting to touch for up to an hour. No brain attached.
So, would you want a brain in each arm? Tell me below.
